title: The Detection of a Hot Molecular Core in the Large Magellanic Cloud with ALMA
question: Does the high-mass YSO ST11 in the LMC host a hot molecular core, and how do its molecular abundances compare with Galactic hot cores?

what.value: Orion KL spectral line data for comparison rotation diagram

evidence.quote: The Orion data is obtained with the 20$\ensuremath{''}$ beam size ($\sim$0.04 pc at the Orion region) and adopted from (cite: Schi97).
We use the following isotope abundances for ST11; $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C = 49, $^{16}$O/$^{17}$O = 3400, and $^{32}$S/$^{34}$S = 15, according to (cite: Wan09)

what.value: Dust opacity of grains with thin ice mantles

evidence.quote: We use the mass absorption coefficient of dust grains coated by thin ice mantles as presented in (cite: Oss94).

what.value: Galactic hot core abundances (Orion, W3(H2O), G34.3+0.15)

evidence.quote: $^b$(cite: Ziu91; Sut95; Schi97), also see $\S$ [5.2](#sec_X_mol); $^c$(cite: Hel97); $^d$(cite: Mac96)

recipe.method: Spectra and continuum flux taken from a 0.5" diameter circular region at the 840 um continuum peak after uvcontsub
Single Gaussian fit per line (double Gaussian for blended NO); CO by visual estimate and direct integration 230–285 km/s
Optically thin LTE rotation diagram, straight-line fit of ln(Nu/gu) vs Eu/k
LTE optically thin with Trot fixed; upper limits with FWHM 6 km/s
assumptions: Same region as SO2; Trot = 100 K

recipe.goal: H2 column density and gas mass from dust continuum
recipe.method: Optically thin dust emission, N_H2 = (F/Omega)/(2 kappa B(Td) Z mu mH)
assumptions: Td = 40 K, Z = 0.0027, mu = 1.41, Ossenkopf & Henning ice-coated opacity

recipe.method: Integrate interpolated SED 1–1000 um; Robitaille Online SED Fitter on 2–840 um data excluding SPIRE 350/500
assumptions: Distance to ST11 equals LMC distance

recipe.goal: Fractional abundances vs Galactic hot cores
recipe.method: N(X)/N(H2) with LMC isotope ratios; Galactic sources re-estimated with local ISM ratios
Blue wing 230.5–240.5 km/s, red wing 265.5–285.5 km/s; mass from CO intensity conversion factor; timescale from 0.24 pc / 20 km/s
key_parameters: Conversion factor 8.8 Msun (K km/s)^-1 pc^-2; S/N > 6

evidence.quote: This H$_2$ column density corresponds to the total gas mass of 115 M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ in the line of sight.
The bolometric luminosity of ST11 is estimated to be 5 $\times$ 10$^5$ L$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$
The estimated stellar mass of ST11 in the best-fit model is 50 M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$.
The derived outflow mass is $M_{\mathrm{out}}$ = 74 M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$
we can roughly estimate an upper limit on the dynamical timescale of the outflow, which is about 10$^4$ years

not_stated_but_needed: tclean/clean parameters (weighting, robust, deconvolver, masking, image size, cell size)
line-free channels used for uvcontsub and local baseline
how the 359 GHz continuum band was defined and its bandwidth
how the 840 um flux of 23.2 mJy was converted from the 0.34 Jy/beam
on-source times (Table 1 time column is empty)
score_reason: Data public and analysis mostly explicit with tabulated line parameters, but imaging details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, Gaussian line fits and rotation diagrams with numeric results are redoable from Table 1 recipes.
